finding: #1925 H1. 7491 card_catalog rows from hobbymonitor-2026-09-04 under basketball/topps-royalty carry year 2025 while their own setName states 2023. The census compared 5,381 card numbers across all 28 products: 5,351 agree with the year-N checklist, 444 agree with year N+1, and ZERO agree with N+1 but not N — so the setName is right and the year field is wrong. This file is part 04 of 8 for this product: 1000 retire, 0 reslug.
rulings: THE CHECKLIST IS THE AUTHORITY AND THE setName IS RIGHT. Every number-to-player comparison in #1925 resolves to year N. A row is retired only where the year-N address is already held by the SAME player from a CHECKLIST source (CF-COUNT-BY-SOURCE-NOT-ROW-COUNT); a twin from `ingest-auto-seed` or `bccp` earns no delete and is excluded instead.

THE SALES DO NOT MOVE — `keepSales: true`. 7,905 sales rest on these rows' slugs and their titles are 7,901-to-0 the year-N+1 product: they belong to the card that STAYS, not the one that moves. moveCatalogRow re-points a row's own sales by default, which here would carry genuine year-N+1 sales back to year N — the exact mispricing this repair exists to end. Under the flag the lane hands moveCatalogRow no salesContainer, so hobbyiqCardId and cardId are untouched and the rematch re-derives them against the genuine year-N+1 identity. Measured: 7,776 of the 7,905 have a genuine year-N+1 row at their card number to land on; 129 do not and need a checklist ingest first.

RETIRE IS A HARD DELETE, AND IT IS ORDERED FIRST. card_catalog has no field that stops a row resolving, so a retire deletes the row and its graded children, and leaves its sales UNPLACED. Retires sort before reslugs in every file, and the files sort in the order they must run.

AN OCCUPIED DESTINATION IS REPORTED, NEVER ROUTED AROUND. 5,899 rows whose year-N destination names a DIFFERENT player, and 712 whose destination is an UNNAMED bccp row, are in docs/reports/2026-09-07-hobbymonitor-year-excluded.md and in no list.
